messages:
kira (AE): FYI prospect Plexa's POC is showing slow first-token times — ~1.1s on average, they expected <300ms. Started after we moved them to dedicated pool this morning. Can we swarm? Also they're asking committed pricing options.

sam (SE): Thanks. Which model and are they using streaming or blocking calls? Any sample request payload + headers (client concurrency)?

kira (AE): model=redwood-1-large, using streaming; client is Node SDK with concurrency 6. Payload is mostly ~40-80 token prompts. Quick curl they ran: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ....' -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Summarize...","stream":true}'``` They pasted a short timeline: first token ~1.1s, subsequent tokens ~30ms.

lee (eng-oncall): Pinging infra. Can you paste the request IDs? I'll pull the backend trace.

kira (AE): one req id: r-6a12f3b4. customer also said sometimes they see 429s when spiking bursts.

lee (eng-oncall): pulled logs for r-6a12f3b4 -> show repeated kvcache MISS entries and batching latency accumulating. Here's relevant snippet: ```[2026-03-21T14:05:03Z] req=r-6a12f3b4 route=dedicated-pool-03 batch_wait_ms=120 batch_size=1 kvcache=MISS kernel=quant_fp16 first_token_ms=1120``` Looks like min_batch_delay configured at 100ms on that pool, and because many single-message clients arrive with slight jitter, the runtime waits and ends up serving tiny batches after the delay. Streaming also adds some backpressure.

sam (SE): That log points to two interacting issues: (1) batching delay + low parallelism -> high TTFT; (2) KV cache not primed because different client shards/contexts or they restart pods often.

devops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler triggered burst nodes +3 at 14:04:58Z for pool dedicated-pool-03.

oliver (security): quick Q for presales pack: do we need to call out any dedicated-pool data residency or encryption caveats for Plexa (they asked in the questionnaire). I can draft an answer if someone confirms storage of KV cache is ephemeral.

lee (eng-oncall): KV cache is ephemeral per inference node and NOT persisted across restarts for this customer's private config (confirmed). I'll add that to security answer.

sam (SE): Immediate mitigations to propose to Plexa: 
- reduce pool "min_batch_delay" from 100ms -> 20ms to favor latency over batching efficiency
- lower "min_batch_size" to 1 and enable "prefer_immediate":true for latency-sensitive routes
- enable KV prefill on warmup (prefetch top prompt prefixes) or run a tiny warmup job at test start
- advise client to use short parallel warmup hits (2-3 concurrent warmup requests) rather than serial cold calls

kira (AE): I'll propose the above and ask if they'd accept a short change window to tune the pool. Also they asked about committed pricing tiers for Dedicated. Can someone flag pricing?

sam (SE): For committed reserved capacity pricing — handoff to sales ops, but for technical presales note that lowering min_batch_delay will slightly increase unit token cost because batching efficiency drops. Give them an L0 estimate: expect ~5-15% higher tokens/sec cost with 20ms delay vs 100ms depending on workload.

maya (customer): Thanks team — we can try the tuning. We can run a 1-hour test with your changes. Also, any quick workaround on our side to reduce latency now?

sam (SE): Short-term on your side: (1) send a tiny parallel warmup of 4 requests before traffic; (2) switch to polling non-streaming for first-token sensitive flows (streaming has small overhead on our side in some cases); (3) ensure your client reuses connections and doesn't re-open TLS per req.

lee (eng-oncall): I'll apply a temporary pool override for dedicated-pool-03: min_batch_delay=20ms prefer_immediate=true and kick the warmup job at 14:18Z. Will monitor traces and post results in 10m.

devops-bot: ACTION: pool-override applied to dedicated-pool-03 by lee at 14:12Z.

lee (eng-oncall): After override, sampled trace r-6a13f7c2 -> first_token_ms=220 batch_size=1 kvcache=HIT. Looks much better. ```[2026-03-21T14:16:40Z] req=r-6a13f7c2 first_token_ms=220 batch_wait_ms=18 kvcache=HIT```

maya (customer): Seeing ~230ms on our side for first token now. Big improvement — thank you. Can you also confirm that KV cache is ephemeral for our compliance questionnaire?

oliver (security): Confirmed: KV cache is in-memory per-node, ephemeral, encrypted in transit, not persisted to disk. I'll send formal language for the questionnaire and attach to this thread.

kira (AE): Great. Next steps: I'll schedule 1-hr tuned run with Plexa at 15:00 and loop in sales-ops for committed pricing. Thanks team :thumbsup:

maya (customer): Awesome — we appreciate the fast swarming.

sam (SE): Follow-up: I'll prepare a quick doc summarizing the latency vs cost tradeoffs and include recommended defaults for future POCs.
